function: Hierarchical multi-agent TD3 learns LEO and HAP transmit power, bandwidth, computing allocation and SemCom/BitCom mode selection to maximize long-term hybrid communication effectiveness in two-hop NTN downlinks (p. 15, 17-18).
system: Two-hop NTN: one LEO satellite (700 km), 3-5 HAPs, 10-50 users; scalar antenna gains only, no arrays or RIS; 20 GHz LEO-HAP, 2 GHz HAP-user (p. 21-22).
method: Hierarchical multi-agent TD3 (LEO high-level agent, HAP low-level agents, Gumbel-Softmax mode selection), online reinforcement learning; ViT semantic codec pretrained offline with MSE loss, then fixed (p. 8, 17-19).
data_channel: Own simulator following 3GPP TR 38.811/38.821: free-space and atmospheric loss, log-normal shadowing, blockage, LoS LEO-HAP, Rician HAP-user fading; Kodak24 and EuroSAT images (p. 6-7, 22).
test_conditions: DRL trained 1000 episodes, evaluated in same simulated NTN over SNR -10 to 30 dB, 5-35 users, HAP count, resource sweeps; no unseen scenario or dataset stated (p. 22-28).
baselines: Learned: conventional TD3-SBRA, MASAC-SBRA, HMADDPG-SBRA; non-learned: equal allocation with random mode, random policy; also SemCom-only, BitCom-only variants and JPEG/JPEG2000 BitCom (p. 21).
metrics: Average HCE, training reward, latency satisfaction rate (CDF), PSNR, SSIM, latency versus data size, mode-switching frequency, FLOP-based execution time (p. 22-29).
complexity: Per-step order O_Total(t) (Eq. 55) linear in users, HAPs, batch and network sizes; Table 3 compares baselines; FLOP-based execution time in Fig. 17 (p. 20-21, 28-29).
q1_support: p. 6: "We adopt 3GPP Technical Report (TR) 38.811 and TR 38.821 NTN channel models"; also p. 6: "using the 3GPP TR 38.811 blockage model". The LEO-HAP and HAP-user links of the DRL environment are built on these models (p. 6-7); the Rician A2G fading is custom and the codec PSNR/SSIM figures use AWGN (p. 26).
q2_support: p. 22: "the approach is expected to generalize to other datasets with similar image resolution and semantic content" is an expectation, not a test; p. 19: "the semantic model remains fixed after training, while the RL policy dynamically adjusts resource allocations". Only SNR, user-density, HAP-count and resource sweeps are reported (p. 23, 28); no model trained in one condition and tested in another.
q3_support: p. 21: "Heuristic Equal Allocation (EA), which statically assigns power, bandwidth, and computation resources" (non-learned) and "Multi-Agent Soft Actor-Critic for SBRA (MASAC-SBRA)" plus HMADDPG-SBRA (learned); p. 23: "with the proposed HMATD3-SBRA achieving the highest HCE among all benchmarks".
q4_support: p. 20: "computational complexity of HMATD3-SBRA can be decomposed into three main components" with the total per-step order in Eq. (55) and Table 3 (p. 21); p. 28: "estimated number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) per training update".
q5_support: p. 22: "the EuroSAT dataset [83], which contains satellite images of land use/cover types" and Kodak24 are public image sets of the learning task alone, and the channel is simulated (p. 6-7); no code or data link is given anywhere, so not met.
notes: Include; page 1 holds the title Hybrid Semantic-Bit Communications for NTN Downlinks: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent DRL Approach, matching the DOI. Area 6: the learned DRL controls transmit power and bandwidth of LEO-HAP-user satellite links jointly with computing allocation and SemCom/BitCom mode (p. 15, 17), which Step 1 rule 4 keeps as physical layer; the ViT semantic codec is the service carried, not the function graded. NTN works admit single-antenna links. Judgement call for the reviewer: q1 is 1 because the paper says it adopts TR 38.811 and TR 38.821 (p. 6); the A2G small-scale fading is Rician and the codec figures use AWGN, so confirm that the 3GPP statement is enough.
